thought: I have confirmed the defect by reading the file. In `Inventory.reserve` (pyshop/inventory.py:16-23), the guard on line 20 uses a strict comparison `self.available(sku) > qty`. When a customer requests exactly the remaining units (available == qty, e.g. reserve("A", 3) with stock 3 and 0 reserved), the condition is False, execution falls into the else branch on line 23, and OutOfStock is raised even though stock suffices. This contradicts the method's own docstring (line 17: 'Reserving exactly the remaining quantity is allowed'), the README domain rule ('Reserving exactly the remaining stock is allowed'), and tests/test_inventory.py:12-15. `available()` (lines 13-14) computes stock minus reserved correctly, and `release`/`restock` are unrelated, so the off-by-one in the comparison is the sole root cause: it must be `>=`. No further evidence is needed.
